(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for eight to eighteen years if he causes death by the act referred to in paragraph 1.

Failure to Provide Assistance

(1) Whoever fails to provide necessary assistance to a person who is in danger of death or shows signs of serious health disorder or other serious illness, although he can do so without danger to himself or another, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years.

(2) Whoever fails to provide necessary assistance to a person who is in danger of death or shows signs of serious health disorder or serious illness, although he is obliged to provide such assistance by the nature of his employment, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three years or prohibition of activity.

Failure to Provide Assistance by a Driver of a Vehicle

A driver of a vehicle who, after a traffic accident in which he was involved, fails to provide necessary assistance to a person who suffered injury to health in the accident, although he can do so without danger to himself or another, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to five years or prohibition of activity.

Spreading of Contagious Human Disease

(1) Whoever intentionally causes or increases the danger of introduction or spreading of a contagious disease in humans shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to three years, prohibition of activity or forfeiture of a thing.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) he commits such an act during a state of threat to the state or during a state of war, during a natural disaster or other event seriously threatening the life or health of people, public order or property,
c) he breaches by such an act an important duty arising from his employment, profession, position or function or imposed on him by law, or
d) he causes by such an act serious injury to health.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for three to ten years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 serious injury to health to at least two persons or death.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death to at least two persons.

Spreading of Contagious Human Disease by Negligence

(1) Whoever by negligence causes or increases the danger of introduction or spreading of a contagious disease in humans shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year, prohibition of activity or forfeiture of a thing.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to three years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 during a state of threat to the state or during a state of war, during a natural disaster or other event seriously threatening the life or health of people, public order or property,
b) he breaches by such an act an important duty arising from his employment, profession, position or function or imposed on him by law, or
c) he causes by such an act serious injury to health.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one to six years if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death, or
b) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 2(b) serious injury to health.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years if he commits the act referred to in paragraph 3 because he grossly breached laws for the protection of public health.

(5) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for three to ten years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death to at least two persons because he grossly breached regulations for the protection of public health.

Common Provision

The Government shall determine by regulation what is considered to be contagious human diseases.

Endangerment by Venereal Disease

Whoever exposes another, even by negligence, to the danger of infection with a venereal disease shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year.

Endangering Health by Defective Foodstuffs and Other Items

(1) Whoever, in breach of another legal regulation, has for sale or produces for this purpose or procures for himself or another intentionally foodstuffs or other items whose consumption or use for the usual purpose is dangerous to human health shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years, prohibition of activity or forfeiture of a thing.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) he commits such an act during a state of threat to the state or during a state of war, during a natural disaster or other event seriously threatening the life or health of people, public order or property,
c) he breaches by such an act an important duty arising from his employment, profession, position or function or imposed on him by law, or
d) he causes by such an act serious injury to health.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for three to ten years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 serious injury to health to at least two persons or death.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death to at least two persons.

Endangering Health by Defective Foodstuffs and Other Items by Negligence

(1) Whoever, in breach of another legal regulation, has for sale or produces for this purpose or procures for himself or another by negligence foodstuffs or other items whose consumption or use for the usual purpose is dangerous to human health shall be punished by imprisonment for up to six months, prohibition of activity or forfeiture of a thing.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 during a state of threat to the state or during a state of war, during a natural disaster or other event seriously threatening the life or health of people, public order or property,
b) he breaches by such an act an important duty arising from his employment, profession, position or function or imposed on him by law, or
c) he causes by such an act serious injury to health.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one to five years if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death, or
b) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 2(b) serious injury to health.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years if he commits the act referred to in paragraph 3(a) because he grossly breached hygienic or other laws relating to such foodstuffs or items.

(5) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for three to ten years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death to at least two persons because he grossly breached hygienic or other laws relating to such foodstuffs or items.

Affray

(1) Whoever intentionally endangers the life or health of another by participating in an affray shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to five years or a fine if serious injury to health is caused to another in the act referred to in paragraph 1.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years if death is caused to another in the act referred to in paragraph 1.

Criminal Offences Against Pregnancy of a Woman

Unlawful Termination of Pregnancy Without Consent of the Pregnant Woman

(1) Whoever artificially terminates the pregnancy of a pregnant woman without her consent shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for three to ten years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 on a woman under eighteen years of age,
b) he commits such an act using violence, threat of violence or threat of other serious harm,
c) he commits such an act by abusing the distress or dependence of the pregnant woman,
d) he commits such an act repeatedly, or
e) he causes by such an act serious injury to health.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 serious injury to health to at least two persons or death.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for eight to sixteen years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death to at least two persons.

Unlawful Termination of Pregnancy With Consent of the Pregnant Woman

(1) Whoever, with the consent of a pregnant woman, artificially terminates her pregnancy otherwise than in a manner permissible under the law on artificial termination of pregnancy shall be punished by imprisonment for one to five years or prohibition of activity.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 on a woman under eighteen years of age,
b) he obtains by such an act for himself or another substantial benefit,
c) he commits such an act systematically, or
d) he causes by such an act serious injury to health.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for three to ten years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 serious injury to health to at least two persons or death.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death to at least two persons.

Assisting a Pregnant Woman to Artificially Terminate Pregnancy

(1) Whoever assists a pregnant woman so that
a) she herself artificially terminates her pregnancy, or
b) she requests another or permits another to artificially terminate her pregnancy otherwise than in a manner permissible under the law on artificial termination of pregnancy,
shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to five years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 towards a woman under eighteen years of age, or
b) he contributes by such an act to serious injury to health of the pregnant woman.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one to six years if he contributes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 to the death of the pregnant woman.

Inducing a Pregnant Woman to Artificially Terminate Pregnancy

(1) Whoever induces a pregnant woman so that
a) she herself artificially terminates her pregnancy, or
b) she requests another or permits another to artificially terminate her pregnancy otherwise than in a manner permissible under the law on artificial termination of pregnancy,
shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to five years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 towards a woman under eighteen years of age,
b) he commits such an act by abusing the distress or dependence of the pregnant woman, or
c) he contributes by such an act to serious injury to health of the pregnant woman.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one to six years if he contributes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 to the death of the pregnant woman.

Common Provision

A pregnant woman who herself artificially terminates her pregnancy or requests another to do so or permits him to do so is not punishable for such an act, not even under the provisions on instigators and accomplices.

Criminal Offences Related to Unauthorised Handling of Human Tissues and Organs, Human Embryo and Human Genome

Unauthorised Removal of Tissues and Organs

(1) Whoever, in breach of another legal regulation, performs on another a removal of tissue, cell or organ from his body shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years.

(2) The same punishment shall be imposed on whoever, in breach of another legal regulation, procures, mediates, offers, imports, exports or transports for himself or another removed human tissue, cell or removed human organ from the body of a living person, or otherwise handles such tissue, cell or organ.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years or forfeiture of property if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 on a child,
b) he commits such an act using violence, threat of violence or threat of other serious harm,
c) he commits such an act by abusing distress or dependence,
d) he commits such an act on at least two persons,
e) he commits such an act repeatedly,
f) he commits such an act as a member of an organised group,
g) he causes by such an act serious injury to health, or
h) he obtains by such an act for himself or another substantial benefit.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for eight to sixteen years or forfeiture of property if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 on a child under fifteen years of age,
b) he commits such an act in connection with an organised group operating in more than one state,
c) he causes by such an act death, or
d) he obtains by such an act for himself or another benefit on a large scale.

Unlawful Handling of Tissues and Organs

(1) Whoever, in breach of another legal regulation, performs a removal of tissue, cell or organ from the body of a dead person shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years or prohibition of activity.

(2) The same punishment shall be imposed on whoever handles removed human tissue, cell or removed human organ in breach of another legal regulation with the intention of enriching himself or another.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one to five years or forfeiture of property if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 repeatedly,
b) he commits such an act as a member of an organised group, or
c) he obtains by such an act for himself or another substantial benefit.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years or forfeiture of property if
a) he obtains by the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 for himself or another benefit on a large scale, or
b) he commits such an act in connection with an organised group operating in more than one state.

Removal of Tissue, Organ and Performance of Transplantation for Remuneration

(1) Whoever, in breach of another legal regulation, offers, promises or provides to another or for another remuneration for the removal of tissue or organ from his body or for the performance of a transplantation shall be punished by imprisonment for up to five years.

(2) The same punishment shall be imposed on whoever, himself or through another, in connection with the removal of tissue or organ or with the performance of a transplantation, requests, accepts or has promised for himself or another remuneration in breach of another legal regulation.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for three to ten years or forfeiture of property if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 as a member of an organised group,
b) serious injury to health occurs in connection with such an act, or
c) such an act is committed towards a child.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years or forfeiture of property if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 in connection with an organised group operating in more than one state,
b) death occurs in connection with such an act, or
c) he commits such an act towards a child under fifteen years of age.

Unlawful Handling of Human Embryo and Human Genome

(1) Whoever, in breach of another legal regulation,
a) uses for research a human embryo or a larger quantity of human embryonic stem cells or their lines,
b) imports or exports a human embryo or a larger quantity of human embryonic stem cells or their lines, or
c) transfers a human genome into cells of another animal species or vice versa,
shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three years or prohibition of activity.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years if he is
a) a person who performs interventions aimed at creating a human embryo for a purpose other than for transfer into a female organism,
b) a person who transfers a created human embryo into the womb of another animal species, or
c) a person who, during research on human embryonic stem cells, performs manipulations with these cells aimed at creating a new human individual (reproductive cloning).

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for three to eight years or forfeiture of property if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 as a member of an organised group,
b) he commits such an act repeatedly, or
c) he obtains by such an act for himself or another substantial benefit.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years or forfeiture of property if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 in connection with an organised group operating in more than one state, or
b) he obtains by such an act for himself or another benefit on a large scale.

CRIMINAL OFFENCES AGAINST FREEDOM AND RIGHTS TO PROTECTION OF PERSONALITY, PRIVACY AND SECRECY OF CORRESPONDENCE

Criminal Offences Against Freedom

Trafficking in Human Beings

(1) Whoever induces, procures, hires, lures, entices, transports, conceals, detains, receives or hands over a child so that it may be used
a) by another for sexual intercourse or other forms of sexual abuse or harassment or for the production of pornographic work,
b) by another for the removal of tissue, cell or organ from its body,
c) for service in armed forces,
d) for slavery or serfdom, or
e) for forced labour or other forms of exploitation, or
whoever profits from such conduct,
shall be punished by imprisonment for two to ten years.

(2) The same punishment shall be imposed on whoever, using violence, threat of violence or other serious harm or deceit or by abusing his error, distress or dependence, induces, procures, hires, lures, entices, transports, conceals, detains, receives or hands over a person other than that referred to in paragraph 1 so that he may be used
a) by another for sexual intercourse or other forms of sexual abuse or harassment or for the production of pornographic work,
b) by another for the removal of tissue, cell or organ from his body,
c) for service in armed forces,
d) for slavery or serfdom, or
e) for forced labour or other forms of exploitation, or
whoever profits from such conduct.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years or forfeiture of property if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 as a member of an organised group,
b) he exposes by such an act another to danger of serious injury to health or death,
c) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another substantial benefit, or
d) he commits such an act with the intention that another be used for prostitution.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for eight to fifteen years or forfeiture of property if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 serious injury to health,
b) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another benefit on a large scale, or
c) he commits such an act in connection with an organised group operating in more than one state.

(5) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for ten to eighteen years or forfeiture of property if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 death.

Entrusting a Child into the Power of Another

(1) Whoever, for remuneration, entrusts a child into the power of another for the purpose of adoption or for another similar purpose shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three years or prohibition of activity.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years or forfeiture of property if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) he causes by such an act serious injury to health,
c) he commits such an act repeatedly, or
d) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another substantial benefit.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for three to ten years or forfeiture of property if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death,
b) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another benefit on a large scale, or
c) he commits such an act in connection with an organised group operating in more than one state.

Deprivation of Personal Freedom

(1) Whoever unlawfully imprisons another or otherwise deprives him of personal freedom shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) he commits such an act on another because of his actual or supposed race, membership of an ethnic group, nationality, political conviction, religion or because he is actually or supposedly without religion,
c) he causes by such an act physical or psychological suffering,
d) he causes by such an act serious injury to health, or
e) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another substantial benefit.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for eight to sixteen years if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death, or
b) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another benefit on a large scale.

Restriction of Personal Freedom

(1) Whoever unlawfully prevents another from exercising personal freedom shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three years if he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 with the intention of facilitating another criminal offence.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) he commits such an act on another because of his actual or supposed race, membership of an ethnic group, nationality, political conviction, religion or because he is actually or supposedly without religion,
c) he causes by such an act physical or psychological suffering,
d) he causes by such an act serious injury to health, or
e) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another substantial benefit.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for three to ten years if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death, or
b) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another benefit on a large scale.

Abduction

(1) Whoever, by deceit, violence or threat of violence or other harm, abducts another to the Czech Republic or to another state, or induces him to go to the Czech Republic or to another state, or dissuades him from returning from the Czech Republic or from another state, shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) he commits such an act on another because of his actual or supposed race, membership of an ethnic group, nationality, political conviction, religion or because he is actually or supposedly without religion,
c) he causes by such an act physical or psychological suffering,
d) he causes by such an act serious injury to health, or
e) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another substantial benefit.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for eight to sixteen years if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death, or
b) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another benefit on a large scale.

Robbery

(1) Whoever uses violence or threat of imminent violence against another with the intention of appropriating another's property shall be punished by imprisonment for two to ten years.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) he causes by such an act serious injury to health,
c) he causes by such an act substantial damage, or
d) he commits such an act with the intention of enabling or facilitating the commission of a terrorist criminal offence, the criminal offence of financing of terrorism (Section 312d) or threatening with a terrorist criminal offence (Section 312f).

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for eight to fifteen years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 damage on a large scale.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for ten to eighteen years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death.

Taking of Hostages

(1) Whoever takes a hostage and threatens to kill him or to cause him injury to health or other serious harm, with the aim of forcing another to do, omit or tolerate something, shall be punished by imprisonment for two to ten years.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) a child is a hostage in such an act,
c) more persons are hostages in such an act,
d) he causes by such an act serious injury to health, or
e) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another substantial benefit.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for eight to fifteen years if he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another benefit on a large scale.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for ten to eighteen years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death.

Extortion

(1) Whoever forces another by violence, threat of violence or threat of other serious harm to do, omit or tolerate something shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to four years or a fine.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) he commits such an act with at least two persons,
c) he commits such an act with a weapon,
d) he causes by such an act substantial damage,
e) he commits such an act on a pregnant woman,
f) he commits such an act on a witness, expert or interpreter in connection with the performance of their duty, or
g) he commits such an act on another because of his actual or supposed race, membership of an ethnic group, nationality, political conviction, religion or because he is actually or supposedly without religion.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years if
a) he causes by such an act serious injury to health,
b) he commits such an act with the intention of enabling or facilitating the commission of a terrorist criminal offence, the criminal offence of financing of terrorism (Section 312d) or threatening with a terrorist criminal offence (Section 312f), or
c) he causes by such an act damage on a large scale.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for eight to sixteen years if he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 death.

Restriction of Freedom of Religion

(1) Whoever, by violence, threat of violence or threat of other harm,
a) forces another to participate in a religious act,
b) unlawfully prevents another from such participation, or
c) otherwise prevents another from exercising freedom of religion,
shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one to five years or a fine if he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1
a) on at least three persons, or

Oppression

(1) Whoever forces another, by abusing his distress or dependence, to do, omit or tolerate something shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year or prohibition of activity.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to three years if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 substantial damage, or
b) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another substantial benefit.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one to five years or a fine if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 damage on a large scale, or
b) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another benefit on a large scale.

Violation of the Inviolability of the Home

(1) Whoever unlawfully enters the dwelling of another or unlawfully remains there shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to three years if he uses violence or threat of imminent violence in the act referred to in paragraph 1 or overcomes an obstacle whose purpose is to prevent entry.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one to five years or a fine if he uses violence or threat of imminent violence in the act referred to in paragraph 1 and commits such an act with a weapon or with at least two persons.

Violation of Freedom of Association and Assembly

(1) Whoever restricts another by violence, threat of violence or threat of other serious harm in the exercise of his right of association or assembly shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years or prohibition of activity.

(2) Whoever, in connection with an assembly that is subject to notification obligation, resists by violence or threat of imminent violence the order measures of the convener or designated stewards of such assembly shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year.

Criminal Offences Against Rights to Protection of Personality, Privacy and Secrecy of Correspondence

Unauthorised Handling of Personal Data

(1) Whoever, even by negligence, unlawfully publishes, communicates, makes accessible, otherwise processes or appropriates personal data that were collected about another in connection with the exercise of public authority, and thereby causes serious harm to the rights or legitimate interests of the person to whom the personal data relate, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three years or prohibition of activity.

(2) The same punishment shall be imposed on whoever, even by negligence, breaches a duty of confidentiality imposed or recognised by the state by unlawfully publishing, communicating or making accessible to a third person personal data obtained in connection with the exercise of his profession, employment or function, and thereby causes serious harm to the rights or legitimate interests of the person to whom the personal data relate.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one to five years, a fine or prohibition of activity if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 as a member of an organised group,
b) he commits such an act by press, film, radio, television, publicly accessible computer network or other similarly effective means,
c) he causes by such an act substantial damage, or
d) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another substantial benefit.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for three to eight years if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 damage on a large scale, or
b) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another benefit on a large scale.

Damage to Rights of Others

(1) Whoever causes another serious harm to rights by

shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years or prohibition of activity.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for up to three years if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 to another substantial harm to rights,
b) he obtains by such an act for himself or another substantial benefit, or
c) he poses in such an act as an official person.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to five years if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 1 to another harm to rights on a large scale, or
b) he obtains by such an act for himself or another benefit on a large scale.

Violation of Secrecy of Transmitted Messages

(1) Whoever intentionally violates the secrecy of
a) a sealed letter or other document in the provision of postal service or transported by another transport service or transport facility,
b) a data, text, voice, sound or image message sent via an electronic communications network and assignable to an identified subscriber or user who receives the message, or
c) a non-public transmission of data to, from or within a computer system, including electromagnetic emissions from a computer system transmitting such data,
shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years or prohibition of activity.

(2) The same punishment shall be imposed on whoever, with the intention of causing damage to another or procuring for himself or another unauthorised benefit,
a) discloses a secret of which he learned from a document, telegram, telephone call or transmission via an electronic communications network that was not intended for him, or
b) uses such a secret.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to three years or prohibition of activity if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 as a member of an organised group,
b) he commits such an act from a reprehensible motive,
c) he causes by such an act substantial damage, or
d) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another substantial benefit.

(4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one to five years or a fine if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 as an official person,
b) he causes by such an act damage on a large scale, or
c) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another benefit on a large scale.

(5) An employee of an operator of postal services, telecommunication service or computer system or anyone else performing communication activities who
a) commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2,
b) intentionally enables another to commit such an act, or
c) alters or suppresses a document contained in a postal consignment or transported by a transport facility or a message submitted by non-public data transmission, by telephone, telegraph or other similar means,
shall be punished by imprisonment for one to five years, a fine or prohibition of activity.

(6) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for three to ten years if
a) he causes by the act referred to in paragraph 5 damage on a large scale, or
b) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another benefit on a large scale.

Violation of Secrecy of Documents and Other Records Kept in Private

(1) Whoever unlawfully violates the secrecy of a document or other writing, photograph, film or other recording, data stored in a computer system or on an information carrier or other document kept in the private of another by publishing it, making it accessible to a third person or using it in another manner shall be punished by imprisonment for up to one year, prohibition of activity or forfeiture of a thing.

(2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years, prohibition of activity or forfeiture of a thing if he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 with the intention of obtaining for himself or another property or other benefit, causing damage or other serious harm to another, or threatening his social reputation.

(3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to five years or a fine if
a) he commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) he commits such an act towards another because of his actual or supposed race, membership of an ethnic group, nationality, political conviction, religion or because he is actually or supposedly without religion,
c) he causes by such an act substantial damage, or
d) he commits such an act with the intention of obtaining for himself or another substantial benefit.

b) v úmyslu získat pro sebe nebo pro jiného prospěch velkého rozsahu. Zneužití dítěte k výrobě pornografie

b) if he or she commits such an act with the intent to enable or facilitate the commission of a terrorist criminal offence, the criminal offence of financing of terrorism (Section 312d) or threatening with a terrorist criminal offence (Section 312f). Embezzlement
(1) Whoever appropriates another's thing which was entrusted to him or her, and thereby causes damage not insignificant to another's property, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years, prohibition of activity or forfeiture of a thing. (2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to three years if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 and was convicted or punished for such an act in the last three years. (3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one year to five years or a fine if he or she causes greater damage by the act referred to in paragraph 1. (4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two years to eight years,
a) if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) if he or she commits such an act as a person who has a specially imposed duty to protect the interests of the injured party,
c) if he or she commits such an act during a state of threat to the state or during a state of war, during a natural disaster or other event seriously threatening the life or health of people, public order or property, or
d) if he or she causes substantial damage by such an act. (5) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to ten years,
a) if he or she causes damage on a large scale by the act referred to in paragraph 1, or
b) if he or she commits such an act with the intent to enable or facilitate the commission of a terrorist criminal offence, the criminal offence of financing of terrorism (Section 312d) or threatening with a terrorist criminal offence (Section 312f). Unauthorised use of another's thing
(1) Whoever takes possession of another's thing of not small value or a motor vehicle with the intent to use it temporarily, or
whoever causes damage not small to another's property by temporarily using such things which were entrusted to him or her without authorisation,
shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years or prohibition of activity. (2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to three years or prohibition of activity,
a) if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a person who has a specially imposed duty to protect the interests of the injured party,
b) if he or she commits such an act as a member of an organised group, or
c) if he or she causes substantial damage by such an act. (3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one year to five years or a fine,
a) if he or she causes damage on a large scale by the act referred to in paragraph 1, or
b) if he or she commits such an act with the intent to enable or facilitate the commission of a terrorist criminal offence, the criminal offence of financing of terrorism (Section 312d) or threatening with a terrorist criminal offence (Section 312f). Unauthorised interference with the right to a house, flat or non-residential premises
(1) Whoever unlawfully occupies or uses another's house, flat or non-residential premises shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years or a fine. (2) Whoever unlawfully prevents an entitled person from using a house, flat or non-residential premises shall be punished in the same manner. (3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to five years or a fine,
a) if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 as a member of an organised group, or
b) if he or she causes damage on a large scale by such an act. Fraud
(1) Whoever enriches himself or herself or another by misleading someone, taking advantage of someone's error or concealing essential facts, and thereby causes damage not insignificant to another's property, shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years, prohibition of activity or forfeiture of a thing. (2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to three years if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 and was convicted or punished for such an act in the last three years. (3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one year to five years or a fine if he or she causes greater damage by the act referred to in paragraph 1. (4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two years to eight years,
a) if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) if he or she commits such an act as a person who has a specially imposed duty to protect the interests of the injured party,
c) if he or she commits such an act during a state of threat to the state or during a state of war, during a natural disaster or other event seriously threatening the life or health of people, public order or property, or
d) if he or she causes substantial damage by such an act. (5) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to ten years,
a) if he or she causes damage on a large scale by the act referred to in paragraph 1, or
b) if he or she commits such an act with the intent to enable or facilitate the commission of a terrorist criminal offence, the criminal offence of financing of terrorism (Section 312d) or threatening with a terrorist criminal offence (Section 312f). Insurance fraud
(1) Whoever states false or grossly distorted information or conceals essential information
a) in connection with the conclusion or amendment of an insurance contract,
b) in connection with the settlement of an insured event, or
c) when asserting the right to performance from insurance or other similar performance,
shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years, prohibition of activity or forfeiture of a thing. (2) Whoever, with the intent to obtain for himself or herself or for another a benefit, causes or simulates an event with which the right to performance from insurance or other similar performance is connected, or maintains a state caused by an insured event, and thereby causes damage not insignificant to another's property, shall be punished in the same manner. (3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to three years if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 and was convicted or punished for such an act in the last three years. (4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one year to five years or a fine if he or she causes greater damage by the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2. (5) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two years to eight years,
a) if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 as a member of an organised group,
b) if he or she commits such an act as a person who has a specially imposed duty to protect the interests of the injured party, or
c) if he or she causes substantial damage by such an act. (6) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to ten years,
a) if he or she causes damage on a large scale by the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2, or
b) if he or she commits such an act with the intent to enable or facilitate the commission of a terrorist criminal offence, the criminal offence of financing of terrorism (Section 312d) or threatening with a terrorist criminal offence (Section 312f). Credit fraud
(1) Whoever states false or grossly distorted information or conceals essential information when negotiating a credit agreement or when drawing down credit shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years or prohibition of activity. (2) Whoever, without the consent of the creditor, uses funds obtained by a purpose-specific credit for a purpose other than the designated purpose to a not small extent shall be punished in the same manner. (3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to three years if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 and was convicted or punished for such an act in the last three years. (4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one year to five years or a fine if he or she causes greater damage by the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2. (5) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two years to eight years,
a) if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 as a member of an organised group,
b) if he or she commits such an act as a person who has a specially imposed duty to protect the interests of the injured party, or
c) if he or she causes substantial damage by such an act. (6) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to ten years,
a) if he or she causes damage on a large scale by the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2, or
b) if he or she commits such an act with the intent to enable or facilitate the commission of a terrorist criminal offence, the criminal offence of financing of terrorism (Section 312d) or threatening with a terrorist criminal offence (Section 312f). Subsidy fraud
(1) Whoever states false or grossly distorted information or conceals essential information in an application for the provision of a subsidy, grant or repayable financial assistance or contribution shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years or prohibition of activity. (2) Whoever uses funds obtained by a purpose-specific subsidy, grant or repayable financial assistance or contribution for a purpose other than the designated purpose to a not small extent shall be punished in the same manner. (3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to three years if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 and was convicted or punished for such an act in the last three years. (4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one year to five years or a fine if he or she causes greater damage by the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2. (5) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two years to eight years,
a) if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2 as a member of an organised group,
b) if he or she commits such an act as a person who has a specially imposed duty to protect the interests of the injured party, or
c) if he or she causes substantial damage by such an act. (6) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to ten years,
a) if he or she causes damage on a large scale by the act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2, or
b) if he or she commits such an act with the intent to enable or facilitate the commission of a terrorist criminal offence, the criminal offence of financing of terrorism (Section 312d) or threatening with a terrorist criminal offence (Section 312f). Operating dishonest games and bets
(1) Whoever operates a monetary or other similar game or bet the rules of which do not guarantee equal chances of winning to all participants shall be punished by imprisonment for up to two years or prohibition of activity. (2) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for six months to three years if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 and was convicted or punished for such an act in the last three years. (3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for one year to five years or a fine,
a) if he or she causes greater damage by the act referred to in paragraph 1, or
b) if he or she obtains for himself or herself or for another a greater benefit by such an act. (4) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for two years to eight years,
a) if he or she commits the act referred to in paragraph 1 as a member of an organised group,
b) if he or she causes substantial damage by such an act, or
c) if he or she obtains for himself or herself or for another a substantial benefit by such an act. (5) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to ten years,
a) if he or she causes damage on a large scale by the act referred to in paragraph 1, or
b) if he or she obtains for himself or herself or for another a benefit on a large scale by such an act.
