Use of Prohibited Combat Means and Unlawful Conduct of Combat
(1) Whoever during war or other armed conflict or in a combat situation
a) orders the use of prohibited combat means or material of a similar nature or uses such means or material, or
b) orders the conduct of combat by prohibited methods or conducts combat in such manner himself,
shall be punished by imprisonment for two to ten years. (2) The same punishment shall be imposed on whoever, in violation of the provisions of international law on the means and methods of conducting war or other armed conflict, intentionally
a) causes harm to the civilian population or civilian persons in life, health or property by military operation or conducts an attack against them for reasons of reprisals,
b) conducts an attack against an undefended place or demilitarized zone,
c) destroys or damages a dam, nuclear power plant or similar installation containing dangerous forces, or
d) destroys or damages an object intended for humanitarian purposes or an internationally recognized cultural or natural monument or abuses such object or monument for military purposes. (3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for eight to twenty years or by an exceptional sentence if he causes by an act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2
a) serious bodily harm, or
War Cruelty
(1) Whoever during war or other armed conflict violates the rules of international law by treating inhumanely the civilian population, refugees, wounded, sick, members of armed forces who have already laid down their arms, or prisoners of war, shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twelve years. (2) The same punishment shall be imposed on whoever during war or other armed conflict violates the rules of international law by
a) failing to implement effective measures for the protection of persons who need such assistance, especially children, women, wounded and sick, or preventing such measures, or
b) preventing or obstructing civil defence organizations of the enemy, neutral or other state from fulfilling their humanitarian tasks. (3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for eight to twenty years or by an exceptional sentence if he causes by an act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2
a) serious bodily harm, or
Persecution of the Population
(1) Whoever during war or other armed conflict applies apartheid or commits other inhumane acts resulting from racial, ethnic, national, religious, class or other similar discrimination or terrorizes the civilian population by violence or threat of its use, shall be punished by imprisonment for five to fifteen years. (2) The same punishment shall be imposed on whoever during war or other armed conflict
a) destroys or seriously disrupts the source of basic life necessities of the civilian population in occupied territory or contact zone or arbitrarily fails to provide the population with assistance necessary for survival,
b) unreasonably delays the return of the civilian population or prisoners of war,
c) unreasonably relocates or expels the civilian population of occupied territory,
d) settles occupied territory with the population of his own country,
e) recruits children for service in arms, or
f) arbitrarily prevents the civilian population or prisoners of war from having their offences decided in impartial judicial proceedings. (3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for ten to twenty years or by an exceptional sentence if he causes by an act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2
a) serious bodily harm, or
Pillage in the Area of War Operations
(1) Whoever in the area of war operations, on the battlefield, in places affected by war operations, armed conflict or in occupied territory
a) robs the fallen or otherwise appropriates another's property, or
b) arbitrarily destroys, damages, takes away, conceals or abuses another's property,
shall be punished by imprisonment for eight to twenty years or by an exceptional sentence. Abuse of Internationally Recognized and State Symbols
(1) Whoever during a state of threat to the state or during a state of war or during war or other armed conflict abuses the designation of the Red Cross or other distinctive signs or colours recognized by international law for the designation of medical institutions or means of transport for medical assistance or evacuation, shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years. (2) The same punishment shall be imposed on whoever during war or other armed conflict abuses the sign of the United Nations or the flag or state or military sign, insignia or uniform of a neutral or other state that is not a party to the conflict. (3) The offender shall be punished by imprisonment for five to twenty years or by an exceptional sentence if he causes by an act referred to in paragraph 1 or 2
a) death or serious bodily harm,
b) damage on a large scale, or
c) retaliatory measures by the other warring party or the other party to the armed conflict of the same or similar character. Abuse of Flag and Truce
(1) Whoever during war or other armed conflict abuses the flag or state or military sign, insignia or uniform of another state that is a party to the conflict, shall be punished by imprisonment for one to five years. (2) Whoever during war or other armed conflict abuses a declared truce or flag of truce, shall be punished by imprisonment for two to eight years. Injury to a Parliamentarian
Whoever insults a parliamentarian or a member of his entourage, or
whoever unlawfully detains such person,
shall be punished by imprisonment for up to five years. Common Provision
Responsibility of a Superior
(1) A military or other superior is criminally responsible for the criminal offence of genocide (§ 400), attack against humanity (§ 401), aggression (§ 405a), preparation of aggressive war (§ 406), incitement to aggressive war (§ 407), use of prohibited combat means and unlawful conduct of combat (§ 411), war cruelty (§ 412), persecution of the population (§ 413), pillage in the area of war operations (§ 414), abuse of internationally recognized and state symbols (§ 415), abuse of flag and truce (§ 416) or injury to a parliamentarian (§ 417) committed by his subordinate over whom he exercised his authority and control, if, even through negligence, he failed to prevent him from committing such criminal offence, failed to obstruct the commission of such criminal offence or failed to punish him for committing such criminal offence or failed to hand him over to the authority competent for such punishment. (2) The provisions on criminal responsibility and punishability of the subordinate offender shall apply to the criminal responsibility and punishability of a military or other superior. TRANSITIONAL AND FINAL PROVISIONS
Transitional Provision
A sentence imposed before the date of entry into force of this Act for an act that is not a criminal offence under this Act, or its unexecuted remainder, shall not be executed. The provisions on aggregate sentence shall not apply in such case. If an aggregate or cumulative sentence was imposed for such act and a concurrent criminal offence, the court shall proportionally reduce the sentence; in doing so, it shall take into account the mutual ratio of the seriousness of the acts that are not criminal offences from the date of entry into force of this Act and the concurrent criminal offences.
